sections.html:
Three counters in Mount Vernon handle a tax account. The Property Valuation Administration (PVA) sets parcel values; reach it at (606) 256-4194 or write to P.O. Box 977, Mt. Vernon, KY 40456. The sheriff, at 205 E. Main St., Box 2, (606) 256-2032, sends and collects the bills. The County Clerk, (606) 256-2831, Box 6 in the same building, takes over any bill that goes delinquent.

None of the three picks a rate. School and special districts choose their own levies, and the sheriff bills the total. The Fiscal Court meets monthly on the second Tuesday at 1:00 p.m. in the courthouse. Anyone who wants to speak asks for a place on the agenda a day ahead.

Deed and lien searches start at the County Clerk, who holds the county's official records. Trash service and animal control sometimes come up when a house changes hands, and the health department, dog warden and solid waste office each keep a separate number. The Fiscal Court's occupational tax office, (606) 256-8374, deals with employers.

December 31 is the due date under KRS 134.015, and the sheriff collects. A delayed mailing can shift the calendar, but normally the stages go like this.

Rockcastle County sheriff: what a bill costs by when you pay
Payment periodAmount owed
Through November 1Whole bill, less 2 percent
Early November to December 31Printed amount only
JanuaryPrinted amount plus 5 percent
February to April 15Printed amount plus 10 percent, plus a sheriff's fee that Department of Revenue examples include
After April 15Sheriff stops collecting; the clerk takes the bill with a lien attached

Your bill shows which stage applies. Values are fixed as of January 1, so a late winter closing normally leaves the prior year's bill in the seller's name. Before closing day, get an exact payoff from the sheriff.

Mount Vernon is the seat and the largest city, with Brodhead and Livingston as the other towns. The county covers about 317 square miles, partly in the Daniel Boone National Forest, and counts as rural throughout. July 2025 population was estimated at 16,148, up 0.7 percent from 2020. Owners occupy 74.3 percent of homes across 6,534 households that average 2.42 people. A typical home is valued at $123,600, typical gross rent is $676 and midpoint household income is $48,862.

The 2020 count found 7,321 housing units with 10.6 percent vacant, so buyers often have choices. A house with pending repairs or an outstanding lien can be sold for cash as it stands, with the lien paid at closing.

sections.h2: What a median home might cost to carry
sections.html:
Kentucky lowered the 2025 real estate rate to 10.6 cents for every hundred dollars of assessment. School, county and district rates sit on top of that, and only the sheriff's bill for a given address shows the sum.

Older and disabled owners can subtract $49,100 from the assessment. On a house valued near $123,600 that removes a large share of the base, so a qualifying owner gains by filing at the PVA early.

A sale changes who pays. The bill follows whoever held the parcel when the year began, so the contract should assign that year in writing, and any open balance belongs at the closing table.

You cannot file an appeal until you have met with PVA staff, so start there. They must explain the law, the procedure and how your number was derived, and a written record captures your claim and the outcome.

  • Watch for the published inspection notice. The roll opens on May's first Monday and can be viewed for thirteen days.
  • Meet staff in that window, or sooner if an assessment notice has already arrived.
  • File the appeal with the clerk the next workday after viewing ends.
  • Attend the local board hearing, about a month after viewing.

The board considers only evidence presented with both sides there. Insurance papers, construction costs, listings and property descriptions count as proof, and a case with none fails. If the board sets a number above yours after bills are out, a supplemental bill arrives.

Owners 65 and older, plus owners whose total disability is recognized by a federal or retirement program, can take the homestead deduction on their residence. It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. File with the PVA and bring a license, passport or similar proof of age.

An age claim stays in force while the first applicant keeps living there. Most disability claims must be refiled yearly, but people with a service-connected disability and people permanently disabled under Social Security or the state retirement system are excused. A couple counts as one claimant, and a buyer files separately because the break travels with the person.

Churches, schools, charities and governments may be fully exempt under sections 170 and 171 of the Kentucky Constitution, after an application to the PVA.

Delinquency starts when April 15 ends. The sheriff sends the list to the County Clerk, each bill becomes a certificate of delinquency, and the lien in KRS 134.420 lasts eleven years, through any resale of the house.

Interest runs 1 percent a month, and commissions for the clerk and the county attorney follow. The statute puts the sale between three and four and a half months after transfer. A 30-day letter goes out before it, then a second letter if needed, then newspaper advertising of at least 30 days.

A buyer of the certificate may add costs, so paying the sheriff before the April deadline keeps the total small.

A sale does not erase back taxes, but it is a good moment to clear them. Ask the sheriff for a payoff while the bill is still with that office. After April 15 ask the clerk instead, since interest and fees have usually been added by then.

  • Give the payoff figure to the closing agent so it is paid from your proceeds.
  • Search the clerk's records for any lien on the parcel before you sign a contract.
  • Put the year's tax split in writing, because the bill follows the January 1 owner.

A buyer paying cash can skip bank appraisals and repair demands, and the balance owed still comes out of the sale money at the table. Bring your deed, your latest bill and a photo ID to closing. If the house was inherited, have the paperwork showing who now holds title, since the clerk's records must match before anything can be paid off or recorded.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Rockcastle County tax payment?
faqs.a: To the sheriff's office at 205 E. Main St., Box 2, Mount Vernon, (606) 256-2032. The PVA at (606) 256-4194 only sets values and does not collect.

faqs.q: How much does early payment save in Rockcastle County?
faqs.a: Two percent of the bill, when all of it arrives by November 1 on the regular schedule. After that only the printed amount is owed until year end, and penalties begin in January.

faqs.q: What is the older owner deduction in Rockcastle County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, subtracted from assessed value. Owners 65 or older, or with a total disability, apply through the PVA.

faqs.q: When can I speak to the Rockcastle County Fiscal Court?
faqs.a: At its monthly meeting on the second Tuesday, 1:00 p.m., in the courthouse. Ask for a place on the agenda 24 hours ahead.

faqs.q: What if my Rockcastle County bill remains unpaid after April 15?
faqs.a: The County Clerk receives it as a certificate of delinquency with a lien. Interest starts at 1 percent a month, and clerk and attorney commissions are added.
